# DarkRoomLibrary v1.2.7

This security maintenance release restores the repository's existing new-password boundary without changing its domain model or public API shape.

## Changes

- Enforces the existing 8-20 character policy for public registration and administrator-created accounts at both the HTTP validation boundary and the shared service validator.
- Replaces the four regular-expression scans behind four CodeQL alert instances with one bounded pass over the existing ASCII lowercase, uppercase, digit, and special-character classes.
- Preserves the existing rule that any three of the four supported classes are sufficient, including the prior rejection of Java's five default line terminators.
- Adds controller, service, boundary, line-terminator, Unicode-class, and oversized-input regression coverage.

## Verification boundary

- The backend passes `290/290` tests and the 70% JaCoCo gate at `3837/5293` unique source lines covered (`72.49%`, rounded down from the report-level XML counter).
- PR #16 merged the product fix as `ebe01216ca9a843a29cdb7ffa5b384414b9ff894`; exact-commit CI, Security, and Pages all passed, and GitHub automatically marked CodeQL alerts #1-#4 fixed at `2026-08-27T22:14:26Z` without dismissal.
- The release tag still reruns complete CI and requires a successful Security workflow for its exact commit. Public Release assets are not treated as read back until publication completes.
- Existing-login inputs are not narrowed to the new-password maximum in this patch because the repository has no production password-distribution evidence; that compatibility boundary remains explicit.
- Existing single-instance, browser, concurrency, middleware-degradation, and historical three-instance evidence remains dated and is not presented as rerun by this focused patch.
